curriculum.lesson_evidence: A story dance sequence puts movements in order: a beginning that shows the character, a middle where the problem happens and an end that shows the result. A transition is a smooth movement that links two shapes, so the dance flows. Hold the first and last shapes still for a few counts so the audience can see them. Write the sequence with words or stick figures, and count the beats of each movement. Practise slowly and add the speed after you know the order. Stop if you feel any pain.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a six-step sequence for 'The Lost Balloon' with a beginning, middle and end. Include one transition and one held shape.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: '1 Hold the string. 2 Let go and reach. 3 Run after it. 4 Jump to catch. 5 Slow turn to look up. 6 Wave, hold for three counts.' The sequence has a clear order, one transition (slow turn) and a held end shape.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that you should move as fast as possible to show excitement. Clear shapes and smooth links are easier to follow and safer than rushing through the movements.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

WORKED MODEL
Example: sequence for 'The Kite'. Beginning: stand holding a string (held shape). Middle: pull the string, jump as the wind lifts the kite, spin as it tangles. Transition: a slow turn to untangle it. End: wave as the kite flies high, hold for three counts. Written plan: 1 hold, 2 pull, 3 jump, 4 spin, 5 turn, 6 wave and hold.

TRY FIRST
Write a six-step sequence for 'The Lost Balloon' with a beginning, middle and end. Include one transition and one held shape.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: '1 Hold the string. 2 Let go and reach. 3 Run after it. 4 Jump to catch. 5 Slow turn to look up. 6 Wave, hold for three counts.' The sequence has a clear order, one transition (slow turn) and a held end shape.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
